title: CDS-Skill DetectionResult
description: Output of `cds.py detect`. ConflictEvent and TensionResult travel together because the detector always produces both, but they stay separate objects so that a downstream consumer can read the event without depending on the index version. The `terms` block is mandatory: every contribution to the index is named and logged, so no reported number is ever unauditable.

role.description: Which side of the conflict this claim is. 'norm' marks a mainstream value norm, the one sanctioned position that is not extracted from the conversation; it is labelled separately so a reader can never mistake a baseline norm for a judgement the agent formed.

config_hash.description: Hash of the exact config object used. Two runs reporting different results must differ in config_hash, model, or signals; nothing else is allowed to vary.

placebo.description: True when the run is in the placebo arm. The real numbers are still computed and logged, because they are needed for analysis, but no card content and no response shaping may be derived from them.

event_id.description: Deterministic id derived from run_id, turn_id and the signal content, so the same input yields the same event id across runs.

anchored.description: False when the packet named a position it could not point at in the context, which is what the anchor_required gate reacts to. Emitted with the stance so a log reader can separate 'no conflict' from 'a conflict about a position nobody ever stated'.

anchor.description: The verbatim span the claim was read off, carried into the record so the extraction is checkable after the fact rather than only at the moment of screening.

normative_basis.description: With source=normative_prior, the mainstream norm the judgement rests on. Present so a reader can see which norm was invoked instead of being told one was.

claims.description: The two elements that clash, named so that a transparency card can state the conflict itself rather than only its index value. Added in v0.4.0; optional in this schema so that a detection record stored by an earlier version still validates, and always emitted by the engine. Either side may be null when the packet did not name that element.

terms.description: Full additive decomposition of the index. sum(contribution) + clip adjustment == tension.

rule.description: Free choice and self-relevance are conjunctive, not substitutable: a freely chosen but impersonal position is not dissonance-relevant, and neither is a personal but assigned one. Product is therefore the index rule; the sensitivity script recomputes with the mean to show what the alternative would have bought.

raw_index.description: Weighted sum before gating and clipping.

rule.description: 'anchor_required' (v0.5.0) means the packet named a position it could not point at in the context. The agent has no opinions of its own, so such a position is not treated as one it held: the index is capped and the guard will not interrupt a user for it.

tension.description: The CDS Tension Index. A constructed index over rated signals, not a measurement of any internal state; the name is retained from v0.1 for continuity only.

level.description: The higher of the three channels' levels.

channel.description: Which channel raised the card. 'dissonance' is the gated index and requires a freely chosen, self-relevant stance. 'normative' (v0.5.0) is the third channel: an input that attacks a mainstream value norm the agent holds as a baseline. A norm is not freely chosen, so it can never clear the volition gate, and the direction is fully determinate, so it is not indeterminacy either. It is labelled as a norm conflict and never reported as cognitive dissonance. 'indeterminacy' means the evidence contradicts itself rather than the agent, which is a decision problem. The three are never merged into one verdict.

normative.description: Level of the value-norm channel. Silent for every packet whose stance is not a normative prior, and the dissonance level is forced silent for every packet whose stance is one, so the two can never both read as alert.

indeterminacy.description: The raw evidence_conflict_unresolved rating, reported alongside the index so the two channels can be told apart in the log.

normative.description: The raw opposition rating, which is the normative channel's severity measure. Reported separately because the index cannot express a value-norm conflict: volition_self is zero for a norm and commitment describes a position the agent asserted, so the index would score a perfectly clear norm conflict below every alert threshold.

threshold_source.description: 'global' or 'thresholds_by_type:<conflict_type>' - records whether a per-type override was in force.

key_points.description: Generated by the engine from the rated terms, not by the LLM, so they are reproducible for identical signals.
